initial_requirements: UK fishing vessel masters and owners need an onboard electronic logbook that replaces paper recording for regulated fishing activity. The system should capture required logbook, transhipment, and landing information and transmit compliant reports to the appropriate fisheries administration. It should help vessel operators review and submit accurate records while accommodating relevant data supplied by other onboard systems.

topics.topic_content: Onboard users who create, review, and submit records

slots.key: Master and owner responsibilities in the logbook workflow
slots.value: The master should be the main person allowed to create, review, and submit the regulated record, because they’re the accountable operator on board. slots.value: Access should be role-based so the master, crew, owner, shore office, and possibly a compliance user each see only what they need for their job; users should be able to view and amend only the records they are responsible for, sensitive commercial or personal details should be protected from general access, and an audit trail should record who changed what and when. slots.key: Audit trail for record changes
slots.value: An audit trail should capture any creation, edit, submission, correction, cancellation, deletion attempt, and, if relevant for accountability, record views or exports; it should show who did it, when, and from which device or system if that can be determined. Repeated failed submission or login attempts should also be logged, and changes made by support staff or on behalf of the vessel should be clearly marked so it is obvious who actually did what. Access through a shared or delegated device should also be captured, with enough detail to identify the access path: the specific device or terminal, the application or browser used, and whether it was a shared or delegated device. If a device detail cannot be determined reliably, leave it blank rather than guess or record something misleading. Device details should not be shown to ordinary users beyond what is necessary.
